source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Feelings of loneliness, anxiety, or depression related to reduced social contact and interaction, warranting attentive nursing support","B":"A condition generally considered to carry fairly little connection to the experience of being placed on isolation itself","C":"Fairly little psychological impact at all, since isolation is generally viewed as a purely physical precaution","D":"An improvement in mental well-being that would be expected to occur in essentially every client placed on isolation"}}
source_row.rationale: Clients on extended isolation precautions may experience psychological effects, including feelings of loneliness, anxiety, or depression related to reduced social contact and interaction, warranting attentive nursing support, such as regular communication and connection despite physical precautions.
source_row.source_detail: Recognizing Psychological Effects of Isolation Precautions
source_row.source_name: Clinical Psychosocial Nursing References — Isolation Psychological Impact
